clue.text: Excessive exploitation very nearly blocks river

indicators.note: blocks means the shortened word sits in the river's name, obstructing it

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England (several share the name)

indicators.note: very nearly means the word very without its final letter

parts.note: the word very itself

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a river is being over-exploited, almost to the point of being dammed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is an English river; 'blocks' signals insertion, not a dam.
explanation.definitionFit: To overuse something is to exploit it to excess; the noun covers that too-heavy employment.

clue.text: Japan referee lives in new hotel

parts.note: VAR is video assistant referee in football

indicators.note: in places the word for lives between the other two letters

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
is means exists, lives

explanation.surface: A football referee stays in a newly built hotel in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' is not the country but a verb: to japan is to coat with hard black lacquer.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a glossy lacquer, so to japan something is to coat it with a hard shiny finish.

clue.text: It goes round and round most of North Island city

indicators.note: most of means the city's name loses its last letters

parts.note: Rotorua is a city on New Zealand's North Island

explanation.surface: A traveller loops endlessly around a New Zealand city.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotorua, famous for geysers, is on New Zealand's North Island; dropping its last two letters leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: One of five arrivals in small church a supporter there

indicators.note: in places the quintuplet between the letters for small and church

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together

explanation.surface: One of quintuplets, newly born, is christened in a small church with a sponsor present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to the church: the answer is an architectural support found in churches.
explanation.definitionFit: A squinch is an arch built across a tower's corner to carry a dome or spire, a structural support.

clue.text: More costly Father Ted given modern look

parts.note: prices that are up are higher, so more costly
da is a dialect word for father
the name as written

explanation.surface: Father Ted, the sitcom priest, is given an expensive makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is an Irish TV sitcom; here 'Father' gives DA, an informal word for dad, and 'Ted' stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something updated has been brought up to date, refreshed with current style or information.

clue.text: European sophistication

definitions.meaning: second meaning: refinement, elegance of manner

explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter is forced at the start of the word; read lower-case, it means refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a nationality adjective for Poland and also a noun for refined, cultured finish.

clue.text: Sanction unit in renovated art house

indicators.note: in puts the unit inside the rearranged letters
renovated means the building's letters are rebuilt into a new order

parts.note: these words as written supply the letters
I is the roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: Planning permission is sought for a flat in a refurbished arts cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to approve officially, which is what authorise means.

clue.text: Heading across France occasionally to find grave

indicators.note: across means the heading's letters straddle those letters

parts.note: east is a compass heading

indicators.note: occasionally means only some of the letters of France are used

parts.note: alternate letters of France, its second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Someone heads across France now and again to visit a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place, but it is the adjective meaning serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and solemn in manner, which is the adjective sense of grave.

clue.text: Fixing TV show could make others happier

indicators.note: could make means these letters can be reworked into the answer

parts.note: these words as written supply the letters

explanation.surface: A television programme about mending things that cheers its viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a BBC programme in which craftspeople restore treasured family objects.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC series shows experts mending heirlooms, so it is a television programme about fixing things.

clue.text: Worry about cutting paper

indicators.note: cutting means the word for about slices into the paper's letters

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone frets over an item clipped from a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious, a verb synonym for worry.

clue.text: Padding over where arm's held close to body

parts.note: when time is up it is over
a holster is where a firearm (an arm) is carried

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of body

explanation.surface: Instructions on where a gun is carried snug against the torso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' is a weapon here, not a limb, so the place it is held is a gun holster.
explanation.definitionFit: Upholstery is the stuffing and fabric covering on chairs and sofas, the padding of furniture.

clue.text: McIlroy's first club covered constant tiny distance

indicators.note: first means only the initial letter of McIlroy is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of McIlroy

indicators.note: covered means the club's letters enclose the constant

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
c is the symbol for a constant (and the speed of light) in science

explanation.surface: Golfer Rory McIlroy's chosen club stays in its cover, a picture from the course.
explanation.walkthrough: Rory McIlroy is a Northern Irish golfer, which steers the reader toward golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A micron is a micrometre, one millionth of a metre, so a very small length.

clue.text: Refreshed squaddies slept outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for slept goes around the soldiers

parts.note: rested means slept or relaxed
OR is Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers; a squaddie is a private soldier

explanation.surface: Soldiers who slept out in the open wake up refreshed.
explanation.walkthrough: A squaddie is British slang for a private soldier; OR (Other Ranks) covers soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Restored means brought back to good condition, as rest leaves someone refreshed and renewed.

clue.text: Trim fruits in different heaps

indicators.note: in places the fruits inside the rearranged letters
different means the letters of heaps are put in another order

parts.note: the word heaps as written
hips are the fruits of the rose

explanation.surface: Fruit is being sorted into separate piles.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose hips are the fruit here; 'Trim' is the adjective meaning neat, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim as an adjective means neat and in good order, which is what shipshape means.

clue.text: When out of cash, workers split wrapping paper

indicators.note: wrapping means the word for split goes around the rest

parts.note: to part is to split

indicators.note: out of means the word for when is removed from cash

parts.note: the word cash as written
as means when
men are workers

explanation.surface: Short of money, workers divide up the wrapping paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When out of cash' looks like scene-setting but is a deletion: the word for when leaves cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is writing material made from animal skin, or a paper made to resemble it.

clue.text: Fit ground inside city? That's clever

indicators.note: inside means the reshaped letters go within the city's letters

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: ground means the letters of fit are crushed and reshaped

parts.note: the word fit as written

explanation.surface: A fit city sports ground earns praise as smart planning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as a sports field but is the anagram signal; the city is New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty is informal for skilful or neatly ingenious, a synonym of clever.

clue.text: Do without extra small prune left over

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
to pare is to trim or prune

explanation.surface: Skip the extra little dried plum that has been left on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is defined several times over: 'Do without', 'extra' and 'left over' all mean it, as does S plus PARE.
explanation.definitionFit: If you can spare something you can manage without it; spare also means extra or surplus.

clue.text: Architect left one instrument

parts.note: Renzo Piano is an Italian architect (the Shard, Pompidou Centre)
a means one

explanation.surface: An architect leaves behind a single musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The architect is Renzo Piano, designer of London's Shard.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianola is a player piano, a keyboard instrument operated mechanically by perforated rolls.

clue.text: Former coach's conscientious commitment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a public stagecoach, especially in France
second meaning: careful and persistent effort

explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a sports trainer, but it is the horse-drawn kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old European stagecoach and the quality of steady, careful hard work.

clue.text: Badly sullied?

indicators.note: badly means the letters of sullied are jumbled

parts.note: the word sullied as written

explanation.surface: A query whether something has been seriously stained.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: something badly sullied has been mistreated.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-used means treated badly or abused, as something dirtied and spoiled has been.

clue.text: Sanitise lists Anglicans put outside

indicators.note: put outside means the church letters go around the word for lists

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: Church of England members are asked to clean up their lists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' looks like a noun for rosters, but it is the verb meaning tilts.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to make thoroughly clean, which is what sanitise means.

clue.text: Harry a competitor in the Crucible

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Harry ..., the boy wizard
second meaning: a snooker player, one who pots balls, at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield

explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible in Sheffield hosts the World Snooker Championship; a player who pots balls is the answer. Crucible is also this setter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the boy wizard is also a word for someone who pots, as snooker players do.

clue.text: Designs using fine wood particles

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
ash is a tree and its timber
ions are charged particles

explanation.surface: A craftsman makes designs from fine sawdust.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to fashion is to shape or create, so fashions means designs or makes.

clue.text: Case section of canal Egypt added

parts.note: a lock is a gated stretch of a canal
ET is the international vehicle code for Egypt

explanation.surface: A guide to a canal system with an Egyptian stretch tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: A locket is a small hinged case worn on a chain, holding a picture or keepsake.

clue.text: Vice perhaps affected inspiring student

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the word for affected takes the student inside

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected
L is a learner, a student

explanation.surface: Wickedness can seem affected when it inspires a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice' is not wickedness but the workshop tool; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a gripping tool that holds work, one kind of clamp.

clue.text: Drills maybe two poles or rocks

indicators.note: rocks means these words are shaken up and rearranged

parts.note: these words as written supply the letters

explanation.surface: Drilling equipment might be a pair of poles or rocks, a builder's site list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks drills as examples of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric drills are one example of motorised hand tools for workshop use.

clue.text: Make up time lost in first class

indicators.note: lost means the letter for time disappears from the word

parts.note: to atone is to make up for a wrong
T is the physics abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make up for time lost in a first-class carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A1 is an informal term for excellent or top-rate, originally a Lloyd's register ship grading.

clue.text: Wheels shy tourist now and then

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to cast

indicators.note: now and then means only occasional letters of tourist are taken

parts.note: the alternate letters of tourist, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A shy holidaymaker drags a wheeled suitcase now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like timid, but it is the verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Castors are small swivelling wheels fitted under furniture or trolleys.

clue.text: Modified an obsolete piano brought in

parts.note: an gives the article a

indicators.note: brought in means the piano letter is placed inside the word for obsolete

parts.note: dated means old-fashioned, obsolete
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An outdated piano is brought in and reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to alter it to suit; modified and adapted are synonyms.
